description: CexChain protocol objects of specification revision v0.16 (trust nodes), built by an independent Python encoder from spec/README.md (sections 6 and 11) and spec/cexchain.cddl. Times are milliseconds since the epoch. `mechanism_types` lists the six mechanism types in the specification's table order, each with its initial state and transitions (the membership's in the table's order, the others' sorted). `membership_metadata` holds membership metadata (record key 5 of a cexchain.membership/1 record) on its own: `valid` cases, each its deterministic CBOR (`metadata`) and its values (`membership`: the member's ledger id in hex, and the optional keys only when present), the specification's example first; `refused` cases, each breaking one rule of the `membership` CDDL or its limits in section 6, which `why` names: "no metadata" (not a map), "unknown key" (a text key the CDDL does not name, or a key that is not text), "missing key", and the key whose rule is broken: "member" (not a 32-byte id), "kind" (not organization or person), "name" (not 1 to 256 bytes of text), "verified" (not a boolean), "registration" (not 1 to 64 bytes of text), "jurisdiction" (not two upper-case letters, optionally followed by - and 1 to 3 upper-case letters or digits, the whole text), "until" (not an unsigned integer above 0). A key whose value is not of its type, null included, breaks that key's rule. `standings` holds where a membership stood at given times (section 11, step 9): each its registration time, its until (null if none), and its changes in log order, each its registration time and the state it moved to ("suspended", "active", "ended", or "" for the revocation), then cases of a time `t` and the standing there: "not_yet" (t before the registration), else "revoked" (revoked at or before t), else "lapsed" (t after until), else the state the last change at or before t left (of two at one time, the later in the log), or "active". `replay` holds a trust node's log for each hash, in the format of protocol-v0.14.json's ledgers: the organization (HK Trust Ltd) delegates memberships and notices (example.org.notice/1) to a registrar; each statement registers at its `registered_at`; `refused` statements are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at `at`, and break exactly one rule, which `why` names: "role" (a membership takes no endorsement), "own ledger" (a member that is the trust node's own ledger id), "no metadata", the metadata rules above ("jurisdiction", "unknown key", "missing key", "kind", "until"), "state" (a transition not from the current state), "transition" (one the type does not allow: ended takes none, and states of other types are none of a membership's), "mechanism" (a membership neither supersedes nor is superseded), "revoked" (a revoked membership takes nothing more); every refused statement parses. A membership's registration and transitions are statements about the membership only. `memberships` lists the accepted memberships; `records` gives each record's type, state, revocation, registrant, history, and versions, and, for a membership, its values (null for an absent optional key), its registration time, and its standing at `checkpoint_time` (`at_checkpoint`). `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` (signed at `checkpoint_time`) covers it; keys are seed = SHA-256("CexChain test key: <name>"), `seeds`. `bundles` holds member ledgers' evidence bundles carrying membership proofs (key 9), written by hand (tools/testvectors/evidence_suite.py's Forge; keys are seed = SHA-256("CexChain test key: evidence <ledger name> root"), "... log", and "CexChain test key: evidence HK Trust Ltd registrar"). Each `valid` case is a bundle (`bundle`, hex) of the member ledger `ledger`, the verifier's trust list (`trust_nodes`, each a ledger id and the name the verifier gives it), and what the report states of each proof, in the bundle's order (`memberships`): the trust node's ledger id, whether it is trusted, the name the list gives it (null when untrusted: never the trust node's own name), the membership's id, kind, name, verified, registration, jurisdiction, and until (null when absent), its registration time (`registered_at`), the registration time of the bundle's record (`record_time`) and the standing then (`at_record`), and the proof's checkpoint's time (`checkpoint_time`) and the standing then (`at_checkpoint`). Every valid bundle is complete, and so is every proof in it. Each `refused` case is a bundle that fails for the one rule of step 9 or of key 9 that `why` names: "another member" (a proof's membership names another ledger), "nested" (a proof carries key 9), "twice" (two proofs of one membership: the same ledger and record), "incomplete" (a proof whose checkpoint does not end with a state commitment), "not a membership" (a proof of a record of another type, with a membership's metadata), "does not verify" (a damaged proof), "metadata" and "own ledger" (a proof whose log the ledger rules refuse: a membership's metadata of the wrong shape, a membership of the trust node's own ledger), "too many" (17 proofs), "empty" (key 9 an empty list), "not bytes" (a proof that is not a byte string). A refused bundle fails whatever the trust list.
